rows.scope: Drownings in 'Made Bodies of Water' (the report lists dock areas/piers, pools, quarries, drains; the section text also names canals, bathtubs and slurry pits), all intents (accidental, suicide, unclassified), Ireland, five years 2018-2022 pooled, final CSO data. Share is of all 578 drownings 2018-2022.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF; CSO tables VSA35 and VSA29 extracted 01/05/2025), section 'In Focus: Bodies of Water', pp. 32-33
rows.do_not_add_to: Five-year pooled, all intents including suicide: do not add to any single-year count, to accidental-only series (uk-waid-2024, the ireland-location-*-2019-23 rows), or to WHO/IHME totals. Made and Natural are the two parts of the same 578; the dock-area, canal and river rows sit inside them, never add across levels.
rows.note: WSI's own two-way classification of where people drowned, the latest setting split Ireland prints. Per-year values exist only as bars in Figures 19-20, whose labels did not survive text extraction. The fetch tool reported that the printed 141 and 439 do not reconcile exactly with 578; a person should check the PDF, nothing was recomputed here.

rows.scope: Drownings in 'Natural Bodies of Water' (rivers, lakes, beaches, sea rocks, open sea, and bogs), all intents, Ireland, 2018-2022 pooled, final CSO data. Share is of all 578 drownings 2018-2022.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'In Focus: Bodies of Water', pp. 32-34
rows.do_not_add_to: Five-year pooled, all intents: do not add to single-year counts, accidental-only rows, or other countries' splits (australia-location-2024-25, uk-waid-2024, canada-location-*). Contains the rivers row (151); never add rivers to it.
rows.note: The report says the distinction between beaches and open sea is defined by the CSO and that several drownings recorded as Open Sea most likely had a point of entry at a beach. Only rivers is printed with its own count; lakes, beaches, open sea, sea rocks and bogs have no printed count.

rows.scope: Drownings in rivers, all intents, Ireland, 2018-2022 pooled, final CSO data; share of all 578 drownings. The report says 64 of the 151 were deaths by suicide (31% of all deaths by suicide from drowning) and the other 87 were largely associated with land-based activities.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'In Focus: Bodies of Water', p. 34
rows.do_not_add_to: Subcategory of ireland-water-natural-bodies-2018-22 (439): never add to it or to the made-bodies rows. Five-year pooled, all intents.
rows.note: The largest single body-of-water category WSI prints. 'Beaches and lakes combine for 57 (27.3%) of deaths by suicide from drowning' is printed but gives no all-intent count for beaches or lakes.

rows.scope: Drownings at dock areas (report category 'Dock Area'; the section defines made bodies of water as including 'dock areas/piers'), all intents, Ireland, 2018-2022 pooled, final CSO data. No percentage printed.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'In Focus: Bodies of Water', p. 33
rows.do_not_add_to: Subcategory of ireland-water-made-bodies-2018-22 (141): never add to it. Five-year pooled, all intents; the report says dock areas and canals together are 58 (28.1%) of deaths by suicide from drowning, so this is not an accidental count.
rows.note: The report notes one event in which three people drowned at a single dock area. Per-year values are in Figure 19 (not legible in text extraction).

rows.scope: Drownings in canals (report category 'Canal'), all intents, Ireland, 2018-2022 pooled, final CSO data. No percentage printed.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'In Focus: Bodies of Water', p. 33
rows.do_not_add_to: Subcategory of ireland-water-made-bodies-2018-22 (141): never add to it. Five-year pooled, all intents (a large part of canal and dock-area drownings are deaths by suicide).
rows.note: Dock areas (54) and canals (51) are printed as the two most frequent made bodies of water; the remaining made category ('Made Other' in Figure 19: pools, quarries, drains, bathtubs, slurry pits) has no printed count.

rows.scope: Drownings in Natural Bodies of Water in the single year 2018, all intents, Ireland, final CSO data, as printed in the trend sentence of the Bodies of Water section.

rows.do_not_add_to: Single-year count for one setting, all intents: do not add to the 2018-2022 pooled rows (it is inside 439), to the 2022 annual total (100, web table), or to any accidental-only series.
rows.note: The latest single-year body-of-water count Ireland prints. The report frames it as a downward trend from 110 in 2018.

rows.scope: Drownings in the report's action category 'Boating' (recreational and commercial vessels; the sentence is cut after 'motorised and' in extraction), of all 578 drownings, Ireland, 2018-2022 pooled, final CSO data.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'Actions Leading to Drowning 2018 to 2022', p. 28

rows.note: Answers the water-transport question: watercraft drownings are inside WSI's total as a category, not excluded. The Summary Snapshot (p. 24) separately prints 13 (3.5%) of accidental or unclassified drownings as involving watercraft or domestic settings.

rows.scope: Drownings in the report's category 'Domestic' (a home setting involving bath-tubs and similar; the 2022/2023 edition defines it as bath-tubs, sinks, wells, containers, garden ponds and fountains, and troughs), of all 578 drownings, Ireland, 2018-2022 pooled.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'Actions Leading to Drowning 2018 to 2022', p. 28
rows.do_not_add_to: A category of the same 578 drownings as the bodies-of-water rows: never add to them. Five-year pooled; do not add to the 2019-2023 'domestic/pool settings' row (overlapping years, different coding).
rows.note: The Bodies of Water section separately mentions four young children who drowned in pools and bathtubs; pools are classed as 'made bodies of water', not 'domestic'.

rows.scope: All drownings in Ireland 2018-2022, final CSO data, all intents: 351 (60.7%) accidental, 207 (35.8%) deaths by suicide, 20 (3.5%) unclassified. This is the printed denominator of the 2018-2022 setting rows.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'Total Drownings 2018 to 2022', p. 15
rows.do_not_add_to: A five-year total: never add to single-year rows, to the 2019-2023 total (607; four overlapping years), or to WHO/IHME figures (different case definition, includes suicide).
rows.note: The web page's own year table prints 2018-2022 as 145, 125, 106, 102, 100 (headline 'Total' column); the report's 578 is the final-data five-year total as printed, no reconciliation attempted.

rows.scope: Accidental drownings that 'occurred in natural water (i.e., sea/ocean, lakes, streams, rivers, and similar natural bodies of water)', Ireland, 2019-2023 pooled (394 accidental drownings); the page attributes county totals to CSO tables VSA35 (2019-2022) and VSA29 (2023). Accidental only, suicide excluded.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, Drowning Statistics web page (page dated 12 Oct 2026), section '2019 to 2023 Summary of Key Statistics' under 'Rolling 2019 to 2023 Quick Facts'
rows.do_not_add_to: Accidental only, five-year pooled 2019-2023, place coded as in the CSO's ICD-10 scheme: do not add to the 2018-2022 all-intent body-of-water rows (overlapping years, different classification), to single-year totals, or to other countries' splits.
rows.note: This is a place-coded split (natural water / watercraft / domestic-pool / unspecified), not WSI's made/natural classification. 63.5% of accidental drownings carry no place code, so 32.5% is a floor, not the share of drownings in natural water. The latest period with a setting split Ireland publishes.

rows.scope: Accidental drownings 'in boating incidents', Ireland, 2019-2023 pooled, share of 394 accidental drownings. Accidental only.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, Drowning Statistics web page (page dated 12 Oct 2026), section '2019 to 2023 Summary of Key Statistics'
rows.do_not_add_to: Accidental only, five-year pooled: do not add to ireland-action-boating-2018-22 (overlapping years, all intents) or to any single-year count.
rows.note: Confirms water-transport drownings are counted inside Ireland's accidental total.

rows.scope: Accidental drownings 'in domestic/pool settings', Ireland, 2019-2023 pooled, share of 394 accidental drownings. Accidental only.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, Drowning Statistics web page (page dated 12 Oct 2026), section '2019 to 2023 Summary of Key Statistics'
rows.do_not_add_to: Accidental only, five-year pooled: do not add to ireland-action-domestic-2018-22 (overlapping years, different category definition) or to any single-year count.
rows.note: Bath-tub and swimming-pool are combined in one category; the CSO's 2021 code table (ireland-cso-* rows) prints no count for W65-W68.

rows.scope: Accidental drownings 'coded to an unspecified location', Ireland, 2019-2023 pooled, share of 394 accidental drownings. Accidental only.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, Drowning Statistics web page (page dated 12 Oct 2026), section '2019 to 2023 Summary of Key Statistics'
rows.do_not_add_to: Accidental only, five-year pooled. A residual of the same 394 as the other 2019-23 location rows; never add to them. Not a setting.
rows.note: The key caveat for Ireland: nearly two thirds of accidental drownings have no place code in the vital statistics, which is why WSI builds its own made/natural classification from Coast Guard, Garda, coroner and media information.

rows.figure: 607 (394 accidental, 202 suicide, 11 assault or undetermined intent)
rows.scope: All 'drowning incidents' in Ireland 2019-2023, an average of 121.4 per year, all intents: 394 (64.9%) accidental, 202 (33.3%) suicide, 11 (1.8%) assault or undetermined intent. The printed denominator (394 accidental) of the 2019-23 location rows.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, Drowning Statistics web page (page dated 12 Oct 2026), section '2019 to 2023 Summary of Key Statistics'
rows.do_not_add_to: A five-year total including suicide: never add to single-year rows, to the 2018-2022 total (578; overlapping years), or to WHO/IHME figures.

rows.note: Graded A as CSO vital-statistics data in an official parliamentary record; not read from the CSO's own PxStat table VSA35, so a reviewer may prefer to re-read it there. Codes V92, V93, W16, W65, W66, W67, W68 and X92 are listed with blank cells (no count printed, blanks unexplained).

rows.scope: Accidental drowning and submersion (ICD-10 W65 to W74), Ireland, 2021, count and crude rate per 100,000, as reproduced from Eurostat in Table 3 of the same written answer. Accidental only; excludes watercraft (V90, V92), self-harm (X71) and undetermined (Y21).

rows.note: Useful as the ICD-block accidental total that international comparisons (Eurostat) use; it is not a setting split. Reproduced second-hand; a reviewer may re-read it from Eurostat hlth_cd_aro.

rows.scope: Total drownings in Ireland in 2023, final CSO data (table VSA29), all intents: 95 accidental, 32 by suicide, 2 other/unclassified. Males 100 (77.5%), females 29 (22.5%); eight under-18s.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, Drowning Statistics web page (page dated 12 Oct 2026), section 'Drownings 2023' and the 'Drowning Statistics' year table (row 2023: 95, 32, 2, 129)
rows.do_not_add_to: All intents: never add to accidental-only series (uk-waid-2024) or to WHO/IHME. Never average with ireland-total-2023-provisional (78): the final figure supersedes it.
rows.note: The latest FINAL annual total; 2024 and 2025 are provisional. No body-of-water split is printed for 2023 alone; only the activity split in ireland-activity-2023.

rows.scope: Provisional drownings in Ireland in 2023 as printed in the 2023/2024 report (CSO data extracted 01/05/2025): '78 drowning fatalities recorded to date', 64 (82.1%) accidental, 13 (16.7%) deaths by suicide, one unclassified. Superseded by the final 129.
rows.source: Water Safety Ireland, National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022 (PDF), section 'Provisional Drownings in 2023 to 2024', 'Drownings 2023', p. 7
rows.do_not_add_to: A superseded provisional figure kept only to show the size of the provisional-to-final revision: never use alongside ireland-total-2023 (129), never average, never add to anything.
rows.note: The report itself warns (p. 13) that provisional CSO data is historically around 10% lower than final; for 2023 the gap was far larger (78 provisional vs 129 final). Treat ireland-total-2024-provisional and ireland-total-2025-provisional accordingly.

rows.scope: Provisional drownings in Ireland in 2024 (CSO data, subject to change), all intents: 56 (71.8%) accidental, 11 (14.1%) deaths by suicide, 11 (14.1%) unclassified; 71.8% male. rows.scope: 'Drownings in Ireland year to date: 80 - 1.55 per 100,000' under 'Provisional* Drownings In 2025' (provisional CSO data, subject to change), all intents, no accidental/suicide split printed; by province Leinster 27, Munster 23, Connacht 17, Ulster (part of) 13. rows.scope: Activity preceding the 95 accidental drownings in Ireland in 2023 (final CSO data), as listed under '95 Accidental drownings': 45 swimming/bathing; 44 land-based activity (walking, hiking, angling from shore or structure, driving, cycling, playing sport or games); 6 boating. notes: KEY FINDING. Ireland counts where people drown, but not for a single latest year. The latest Water Safety Ireland report (National Drowning Report 2023/2024 with Rolling Report 2018 to 2022, PDF on watersafety.ie, CSO data extracted 01/05/2025) prints its setting split only for the five years 2018-2022 pooled, all intents, in a section 'In Focus: Bodies of Water': Made Bodies of Water 141 (24.2%), Natural Bodies of Water 439 (75.8%), with rivers 151 (26.1%), dock areas 54 and canals 51 the only sub-categories printed with counts; the only single-year body-of-water counts in prose are natural bodies of water 110 (2018) and 71 (2022). The WSI statistics web page (dated 12 Oct 2026) prints a second, differently coded split for accidental drownings 2019-2023 pooled: natural water 128 (32.5%), boating incidents 11 (2.8%), domestic/pool settings 5 (1.3%), unspecified location 250 (63.5%), of 394 accidental drownings and 607 drownings in all. The 2023 (final, 129), 2024 (provisional, 78) and 2025 (provisional, 80) years have no setting split; 2023 has an activity split only (45 swimming/bathing, 44 land-based, 6 boating). A CSO code-level single-year split exists for 2021 (reproduced in a Dáil written answer of 7 Feb 2024): V90 1, W69 5, W70 1, W73 1, W74 50, X71 43, Y21 1, total 102, with W65-W68 (bath-tub, swimming-pool), V92, X92 blank. Status partial because no source prints a per-setting count for the latest year and the per-year chart values in the 2023/2024 report were not legible. DEFINITION OF DROWNING (acceptance check 3). WSI counts ALL INTENTS: its totals are split into accidental, suicide and undetermined/assault/other (web table) or accidental, deaths by suicide, unclassified (report), and the 2021 Dáil table of 'codes which reference drowning' (V90, V92, V93, W16, W65-W70, W73, W74, X71, X92, Y21) totals 102, the same as WSI's 2021 total. Water transport IS included: 'Boating' is a category of the total (7 of 578 in 2018-2022; 11 of 394 accidental in 2019-2023), defined as commercial and recreational vessels. Domestic settings (bath-tubs, sinks, wells, containers, garden ponds, troughs) are included. The data are registered deaths based on coroner's inquests and ICD-10 coded by the CSO (tables VSA35 and VSA29), supplemented by the Irish Coast Guard, An Garda Siochana, coroners and media; deaths of Irish nationals overseas are listed separately (7 in 2025) and are not in the Irish total. Neither WSI document prints the ICD-10 codes it uses; the code list comes only from the Dáil answer. DISCREPANCIES RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED. (1) 2023: the report printed 78 provisional; the web page now prints 129 final. (2) 2021: WSI web table 57 accidental, 44 suicide, 1 other; the Dáil/CSO table X71 43, Y21 1 (both total 102); Eurostat W65-W74 57. (3) The fetch tool reported that 141 and 439 do not reconcile exactly to 578 and that page-18/24 text percentages differ slightly from the county tables; nothing was recomputed. (4) The web page's headline year table (2019-2023: 125, 106, 102, 100, 129) differs from the final-data sex table totalling 607 (126, 112, 121, 119, 129). WHAT A PERSON WITH A BROWSER SHOULD CHECK. (a) Figures 19-22 of the 2023/2024 report (pp. 33-34) for the per-year values of Canal, Dock Area, Made Other and natural bodies by intent, 2018-2022; the text extraction returned the numbers but not their pairing. (b) CSO PxStat VSA35 (data.cso.ie/table/VSA35) for 2022 counts of W65-W74, V90, V92, X71, Y21, which would give the latest final code-level setting split. (c) The ICD code list on the Dáil page (V93 and W16 are not drowning outcomes). Grades: all rows A as primary official or lifesaving-society compilations of official data; the oireachtas.ie rows are CSO data reproduced in an official record rather than read on cso.ie, flagged in their notes. The ledger holds no Ireland rows yet, so all ids are new; the who-data-gaps note can add Ireland to its list of countries with a setting split.
